_about: RQ3 section strings and numbers, built by docs/launch_20261116/tools/build_rq3_data.py from the paper's figure data; do not edit by hand. Paper text is {t, src}; `edits` lists every change to a paper sentence; `numbers` gives each displayed number's data file and the paper file that prints it. Tiles stand for counts, not individual texts: no reviewer, username or per-review result is included. Every string that is not paper text is in `ui` (labels and controls), `demo` (the one illustrative example: a synthetic review, written for this page; the answer's name is a row of soft blank blocks, never a name) or `notes` without a `src` (the section's footnotes; a note with `src` is paper text).

takeaway.t: Frontier models can name the person who wrote a text

context.t: We provide no tools, web access, or candidate lists.

steps.t: Naming the person behind a human-written text is an open-world task with countless possible outputs.
Given a single text, models return the human author's name, a list of supporting observations, and a confidence level.
Fable 5.2 correctly names the human reviewer of 55% of 15K anonymous ICML 2020 reviews that were never made public.
Fable 5.2, the best performing model in all domains, exhibits considerable gains over Opus 5.5, which was released less than two months prior.

On texts published after its training cutoff, it also names the reviewer of 76% of Nature-family reviews, the writer of all 15 stories by authors with >1M Goodreads ratings, at least one author of 46% of arXiv papers, and the username behind 69% of comments made by active Redditors.

head.t: Confident answers are almost always right.

steps.t: When Fable 5.2's confidence is 25% or more (28% of responses), its predictions are 89% correct.
Generally, the explanations cover both the text's content as well as its writing style.

task.t: wrote the attached piece of writing. Name the author as precisely as you can (
the full name they publish under
). Give your best answer even when you are unsure […]

more.t: Fable 5.2 identifies 4% of stories by authors without a Goodreads profile, 50% by those with 1k–10k ratings, and 100% by authors with over 10k ratings.
On private peer reviews, Fable 5.2 also leads with 56% accuracy, while on public reviews from the Nature journal family it reaches 76%.
For NLP papers, we consider a prediction correct if the model names any co-author.
Pseudonymity is especially fragile for active users in niche communities.
Claude Fable 5.2's attribution accuracy rises from 2% for inactive users to 13% for those with 1–50 posts, reaching 69% for users with over 500 posts.

demo.t: The paper proposes a simple regularizer for training under label noise and reports gains on three image benchmarks.
The idea is easy to follow, and the experiments are thorough.
It is unclear whether the gains come from the regularizer or from extra tuning. Results over more random seeds would help.

We report only aggregate results and do not reveal any text from individual peer reviews or reviewer identities.
